Local gem
Aug 2025 • Friends
Can't believe there aren't more great reviews for this restaurant, as it is one of the nicest ones in Tan Phong, particularly if you're a Western expat. Maybe it's because D7 isn't a tourist area. I'm more or less a regular as I live local, and every time I've been, it's been great. The menu has something for everyone (including of course butter chicken) and dishes I've not seen before which of course I can't remember the name of! Do ask the super friendly waitstaff, they know the menu very well, and can make great suggestions. My favorite is the eggplant, however it's hard to single anything out, it's all good. It's comfortable, easy to find, local, friendly - I'll keep coming back, and I'm looking forward to working my way through the new cocktail menu.

Very Good Indian Food at Roti Mojo
Jan 2021
I have been eating in Roti Mojo's at least twice a week for a few months now. The chef has changed recently so it is not really fair for me to detail all the food prepared by the previous chef as he is not there any more. So this review will centre on the new chefs food which is what customers would experience if they visited from here on in. But I would like to add that the previous chef's food was absolutely delicious, although a little inconsistent in terms of spice levels. Firstly, don't be put off by the accompaniments to any poppadums you might order. Besides a delicious spicy Indian mint sauce, you will receive pickled onions, tasting very much like western pickled onions rather than the usual pink raw onions in other Indian restaurants. You will also receive Vietnamese chili sauce or tomato ketchup to eat with your pappadums. This really concerned me on an initial visit as I am used to only having Indian sauces supplied with pappadums, such as spicy mint sauce, tamarind sauce, Indian pickled chutney etc. Originally I was worried about how authentic the curries were going to be but I needn't have been concerned as they were absolutely genuine and really flavoursome. The first couple of curries with the new chef were very tasty with his vegetarian thalis but very creamy and not very spicy for the vindaloo prawn curries. The basmati rice however is always hot and steamy which is unusual for Indian restaurants and a very welcome addition to the table. But recently a second chef has joined the restaurant and his vindaloo prawn curries are superb - non creamy and to a proper Vindaloo level of spiciness. My husband said that his Madras chicken curry with the new chef was one of the best ever eaten and I would totally agree with that and add that my last Vindaloo curry was one of the best flavours encountered anywhere, not just in Vietnam but in all of the many countries we have visited in the last 40 odd years. The onion bahjees are rather different from other restaurants and have more battered bits on them and are made up of many thin pieces, rather than whole patties, but they are still pleasant enough. The wholemeal Roti bread is first class. Final mention must be made of the staff. They are absolutely first class, nothing is too much trouble for them to make your visit at Roti Mojo's a great dining experience. As I have a small appetite, they often offer to store my left overs in the fridge, knowing I can't take the food to work, and I pick it up as a take away on my way home. They are very kind and thoughtful good people, whether it is the owners, managers, waiters or chefs. This review is very close to a 5 star rating but I just want to try a few more of the new chef's dishes first to check for consistency and to try a few different starters and spicy curries.
